crime: When {WITCH_NAME} was six, her mother pulled her by the hand into the waves. She came out coughing and crying, and her mother smiled. "See? You loved it."

In the mansion, another prisoner took her hand every evening after supper and dragged her out to slide on the frozen lake. Then the thaw turned the middle of the lake grey, and only the ice by the far bank still held. The girl pulled her round that last stretch, laughing, then looked down at the hand shaking in hers. "See? You loved it."

The next evening, after dark, {WITCH_NAME} sat on the lounge sofa and, for the first time, silently called her, straight across the grey middle. Out on the lake, the girl felt an unseen hand tug at hers and ran toward it, laughing. The ice gave way beneath her.

The other prisoners had watched {WITCH_NAME} sit still on the sofa by the fire all evening until lockup. She never got up and never said a word. In the trial court, they agreed the girl had strayed onto rotten ice in the dark.

But one prisoner had stood at the lake and sighted along the dead girl's footprints. They ran in a straight line over the grey middle, pointing at the lounge. She hadn't lost her way coming home. She had run to the sofa, because the girl sitting on it had called her.
fields.epitaph: And when at last she was the one leading, she never asked either.
fields.epithet: The Girl Led by the Hand
execution: The execution stand raises a steep slope of ice from the trial-court floor to the gallery. At the top, her hand is set wrist-deep in a block of ice. The block begins to slide, dragging her down the slope by the hand, head first, into the wall of ice at the bottom. She never cries out; her eyes stay on the spectators the whole way down. At the foot of the slope she lies still, her hand still held in the ice.

magic.name: A Tug on the Hand
magic.text: She silently calls someone, and an invisible hand tugs theirs, leading them to her.
